_note: Sources for Form 2 Biology (Batches B2-1, B2-2 and B2-3, Terms 1–3). The answers are authored facts: a Biology teacher must check them.

plant-reproduction.ref: Asexual and sexual reproduction in flowering plants; natural and artificial vegetative propagation (as in Cameroonian Form 2 biology textbooks)
plant-reproduction.supports: Examples of natural organs (bulb, corm, rhizome, stem and root tubers, suckers, leaf plantlets) and artificial methods (cuttings, grafting, budding, layering, marcotting, tissue culture); advantages and disadvantages; the two practicals.
plant-reproduction.checked: General knowledge, not externally sourced: please check the examples, especially the crops named for each method.

flower.ref: Structure of a flower and pollination (insect and wind pollination)
flower.supports: Parts of the flower and their functions; the drawing's eight lettered parts (flower() in science2.js); self- and cross-pollination; features of insect- and wind-pollinated flowers; the dissection practical and the rules of biological drawing.
flower.checked: Standard textbook content; the drawing and the item banks are authored: please check them.

seeds.ref: Fertilisation, the seed, dispersal and germination in flowering plants
seeds.supports: Pollen tube and fusion of nuclei; fate of the flower parts; bean seed structure (beanSeed() drawing); monocots and dicots; agents and adaptations of dispersal with local examples; conditions and types of germination (bean epigeal; maize, pea and mango hypogeal); the two germination practicals.
seeds.checked: Standard textbook content; examples (mango hypogeal, pawpaw epigeal, Combretum winged fruits) from general knowledge: please check them.

plant-pests.ref: Crop pests and diseases in Cameroon and their control (biological and chemical); safe use of pesticides
plant-pests.supports: Pests (aphids, locusts, weevils, rats); diseases (cocoa black pod: fungus; cassava mosaic: virus spread by whiteflies; maize streak: virus spread by leafhoppers); prevention; kinds of pesticides; safety rules.
plant-pests.checked: General knowledge, not opened in this session: please check the causes and carriers named.

food-transformation.ref: Transformation, preservation and preparation of foodstuffs (cassava, maize, millet, milk); yoghurt making with lactic acid bacteria; methods of preservation and cooking
food-transformation.supports: Products (garri, bobolo, water fufu, corn fufu, pap, bouillie, bil-bil, yoghurt, butter, wagashi) and their main steps; preservation by drying, smoking, salting, sugaring, cooling, pasteurising, canning, pickling.
food-transformation.checked: General knowledge of Cameroonian foods (not opened in this session): please check the local names and steps.

nutrition-health.ref: Nutrition-related diseases (kwashiorkor, marasmus, anaemia, goitre, night blindness, obesity); Body Mass Index with the WHO adult classes; energy values of food; balanced diet; solid waste management (avoid, reduce, reuse, recycle, compost, incinerate)
nutrition-health.supports: BMI = mass ÷ height² to one decimal place (science2.js bmi, bmiClass: 18.5, 25, 30); energy = mass × kJ per gram (fat 37, carbohydrate and protein 17); heat to water = mass × 4.2 × rise (heatToWater).
nutrition-health.checked: WHO BMI classes and energy values are standard; computed by code and tested.

physical-social-health.ref: Exercise and rest; drug abuse: alcohol, cigarette smoking (nicotine, tar, carbon monoxide, passive smoking), marijuana and tramadol
physical-social-health.supports: Health and social effects; about one hour of activity a day and 8–10 hours of sleep for teenagers; refusal skills and sources of help.
physical-social-health.checked: Authored from general health education: please check the advice and the statements on the law (tobacco to minors, smoking in public places, marijuana).

reproductive-health.ref: Practices harmful to reproductive health: early marriage, female genital mutilation, breast ironing, induced (unsafe) abortion
reproductive-health.supports: Definitions, causes and consequences; sources of help for girls at risk.
reproductive-health.checked: Authored; the legal statements (FGM forbidden; abortion illegal except in limited cases; protection from forced marriage) are from general knowledge and must be checked against the Cameroon Penal Code (2016).

climate.ref: The greenhouse effect, global warming and climate change: causes, effects (Sahel droughts, Lake Chad) and prevention
climate.supports: Greenhouse gases (CO₂, methane, nitrous oxide, water vapour); human causes; effects; actions.
climate.checked: Standard results; please check the examples from Cameroon.

waste-ozone.ref: The ozone layer (O₃, stratosphere 15–35 km, UV absorption, CFCs and halons, Montreal Protocol 1987); management of liquid waste: latrine types (pit, VIP, pour-flush, WC, eco-san), siting (≥ 30 m from wells, downhill), care of latrines and WCs, hand washing
waste-ozone.checked: Standard public-health guidance: please check the 30 m distance used by local health services.
